column.text: Bitcoin has broken down below $73,000, its lowest level since September, and the selling is coming from institutions. The market is down 4.99% over 24 hours, with $106.9M in long liquidations behind the move. Spot Bitcoin ETFs lost $201.1M on Monday 9 Nov, pushing the seven-day net to -$2126.1M. Ether ETFs lost $184.5M the same day, with a seven-day net of -$705.6M. Solana's Friday 6 Nov outflow was smaller at -$25.1M, with a seven-day net of -$64.7M. Positioning is the problem for bulls. The BTC long/short ratio sits at 2.965, so the crowd is heavily long into weakness. Fear & Greed reads 32, which is Fear. The desk calls this a liquidity crunch rather than clean capitulation. Rising US yields and contracting dollar liquidity are a headwind for risk assets. Hyperliquid whales are net short $692M in BTC and $372M in ETH, while exchanges show net outflows, which suggests coins are heading to cold storage or OTC desks rather than the order book. Headline risk adds pressure. Nvidia's intraday decline has widened to 5% on a shareholder class action tied to Jensen Huang, and Dan Ives puts a 15% chance on his removal, which could mean a 25%–30% valuation hit. Anthropic's IPO, scheduled for next week at $70–$78 per share, targets up to $64.4B raised at a $1.4T valuation. Meanwhile, Bitcoin has slipped under MicroStrategy's $75,451 average cost basis. The playbook stays short. Treat rallies into $75,451 as better-odds shorts until a real mechanism shows up, such as deeply negative funding, a capitulation print, or a failed breakdown. A counter-trend long needs a high-conviction reversal at exhaustion, not a dip bought because it looks oversold. Watch whether the $73,000 area holds through the next ETF prints.
